race_context: The district: the Metropolitan School District of Bluffton-Harrison serves Bluffton and Harrison Township in Wells County. It runs Bluffton-Harrison Elementary (pre-K through grade 4), Bluffton-Harrison Middle School (grades 5-8) and Bluffton High School {idoe_dir}{wboi_ref}. State enrollment counts rose from 1,632 students in 2018-19 to 1,782 in 2023-24, 1,813 in 2024-25 and 1,860 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}. Superintendent Brad Yates reported a K-12 average daily membership of 1,784.37 in August 2026 {bm_2026_08_17}.

The board has five members: Julie Thompson (president), Mike Murray (vice president), Angie Sheets (secretary), Trent White and Tim Drayer {bh_board}{bm_2026_01_12}. Three members are elected from Districts 1-3 and two at large, in staggered four-year terms {enr_2018}{enr_2020}{enr_2022}{enr_2024}{bm_2024_06_17}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 2 and one at-large seat, one member each, matching the state list {in_list}. The District 2 seat was won in 2022 by Bruce Holland {enr_2022}. He resigned in June 2024 after moving, and the board moved at-large member Angie Sheets, who lives in District 2, into the seat {nb_holland}{bm_2024_06_17}. Sheets is not on the 2026 ballot, so Mark Cobb is unopposed for the open seat {in_list}. The at-large seat is held by board president Julie Thompson, who is seeking a third term against Ryan Schisler {enr_2018}{enr_2022}{nb_oct6}{in_list}.

Earlier vacancies: Preston Kaehr, appointed to the other at-large seat in July 2024, won it in November 2024 and resigned in August 2025 {bm_2024_07_16}{enr_2024}{nb_drayer}. Both Mark Cobb and Ryan Schisler applied for that vacancy and spoke to the board about their qualifications on Sept. 8, 2025. The board then appointed Tim Drayer to the seat through Dec. 31, 2028 {bm_2025_09_08}.

Budget and SEA 1: the News-Banner reported on the district's plans after SB 1 (June 2025) and on expected further budget cuts in 2028 (April 2025) {nb_sb1}{nb_cuts2028}. In June 2026 the board chose Veregy for a guaranteed energy savings contract for solar power, and on Aug. 17, 2026 it unanimously approved the project's final scope for the middle and high schools {bm_2026_06_15}{bm_2026_08_17}. The News-Banner reported that the project should lower utility costs and help the district recover some of the operating money it lost to property-tax changes {nb_solar}.

Safety referendum: in November 2023, voters rejected a district school safety tax levy, 58% to 42%, a margin of 107 votes. It would have paid for two school resource officers and a mental health therapist; the district's three schools shared one officer at the time {wboi_ref}.

Staff pay: the board approved a teacher contract in October 2025. In July 2026 the News-Banner reported that one-time stipends would be paid in August: $750 for eligible teachers and other certified staff and $250 for eligible non-certified staff {nb_contract}{nb_stipend}.

Facilities and academics: in August 2026 the superintendent reported that high school paving and high school HVAC work were essentially finished and that the district was awaiting a cost estimate for structural repairs under the pool deck {bm_2026_08_17}. In 2025, 87.7% of the district's third graders passed IREAD {nb_iread}. In January 2026 the board discussed a prospective new accountability model {nb_account}. In April 2026 Thompson reported that the board had been named an Indiana School Boards Association Level 1 Commendable Board for 2025 {bm_2026_04_20}.

Forums: the News-Banner announced a candidate forum for some contested Wells County races on Monday, Oct. 5, 2026, and published a profile of the at-large race on Oct. 6 {nb_forum}{nb_oct6}. Both articles are for subscribers only, and this guide could not read the candidates' statements in them.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board president, first elected in 2018; listed as a Republican {bh_board}{enr_2018}{in_list}.
background: Chief administrative officer and chief nursing officer at Bluffton Regional Medical Center. She lives in Harrison Township, is 64, has served on the board of the Caylor Nickel Family YMCA and is board president of the Wells County Chamber of Commerce {nb_oct6}.

Won the at-large seat in 2018 (1,071 votes among five candidates) and again in 2022 (1,357 votes among three candidates) {enr_2018}{enr_2022}. Board secretary in 2025 and board president since January 2026; she also serves on the board's negotiations committee {bm_2025_01_13}{bm_2026_01_12}.
path_to_ballot: Filed June 16, 2026, listed as a Republican {ic_list}{in_list}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member. As president, she reported in April 2026 that the board had been named an ISBA Level 1 Commendable Board for 2025 {bm_2026_04_20}. She made the June 2026 motion choosing Veregy for the solar energy-savings contract {bm_2026_06_15}.
